prompt: Write a note to a friend about a neighbor's advice about your garden. Aim for about 400 words. Reply with the note only.
final_message:
Hi Marcy,

You won't believe what happened over the fence last Saturday. I was out front wrestling with the tomatoes, which, as you know, have been a sad, leggy mess all summer, when Mr. Okafor from next door wandered over with his coffee. He's been gardening on that lot for thirty years, and he never says anything unless he has an opinion. This time, he had several.

First, he told me I've been watering all wrong. I've been giving everything a light sprinkle every evening, like I'm tucking the plants in for bed. He says that trains the roots to stay shallow and lazy. His advice is to water deeply, twice a week, first thing in the morning, and to aim at the soil rather than the leaves. He swears that's why my squash leaves keep getting that powdery white coating.

Second, he looked at my beds and basically sighed. Apparently I planted everything too close together. I thought I was being clever and squeezing in more food. He says crowded plants fight over light and air, which explains the mildew and the spindly stems. He told me to thin the carrots right now, even though it feels cruel, and to give the tomatoes at least two feet each next year.

Third, and this one surprised me, he told me to stop fussing over fertilizer. I'd been buying all sorts of bottles. He said, "Feed the soil, not the plant," and pointed at my bare dirt. Compost in the fall, a layer of shredded leaves as mulch, and that's it. He offered to drop off a few wheelbarrow loads from his pile, which he calls "black gold" with a completely straight face.

I'll admit I bristled a little at first. Nobody enjoys hearing that they've been doing it wrong for months. But he was kind about it, and he even came back later with a hand trowel to show me how to check moisture by digging down two inches. Honestly, the man knows his stuff.

So I'm going to try all of it next season. I'll report back, and I fully expect to be insufferable if the tomatoes finally behave.

Come over this spring and help me plant? I'll make lemonade, and you can meet the legend himself. Bring gloves.

Love,
[name]
